validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE well-corroborated by FOUR independent-origin primary sources, none of them gem.wiki-derived: (1) Government of Kazakhstan Decree No.1151 of 30 Nov 2007 'On construction of the "Karachaganak-Uralsk" gas pipeline' (adilet.zan.kz/rus/docs/P070001151_), ordering KPO consortium to build it under the Karachaganak PSA; (2) KazInform wire story dated 23 Nov 2007 (republished at online.zakon.kz/Document/?doc_id=30144485) covering the ground-breaking ceremony with PM Karim Masimov; (3) TMK (pipe manufacturer) press release dated 17 Dec 2009 confirming completed delivery of pipe to the KPO consortium 'for construction of the Karachaganak-Uralsk gas pipeline'; (4) Intergas Central Asia's own current (as of 01.01.2025) trunk-pipeline capacity register (intergas.kz PDF) lists it by name with technical parameters and a 2024 utilization figure, i.e. it is an actively maintained, actively reported asset today, not a stale/GEM-only entry. Also corroborated by an ecoportal.kz environmental-hearing filing for Intergas's Uralsk LPU, which lists the exact 0-152.13km service boundary of this line alongside the Soyuz/Orenburg-Novopskov trunks it ties into. No existence doubt at all.

CLASSIFICATION (transmission) holds up. Intergas's own environmental filing (ecoportal.kz, Uralsk LPU) groups 'Karachaganak-Uralsk' together with the Soyuz and Orenburg-Novopskov trunk lines as one of the 'магистральных газопроводов' (main/trunk gas pipelines) the Uralsk LPU maintains, and the 2007 KazInform article describes it tying into the Soyuz/Orenburg-Novopskov trunk at a point near the village of Novenkiy ~15km from Uralsk. It is not a gathering or plant-internal process line — it moves KPO-processed gas from the Karachaganak complex to a trunk tie-in / city gate for regional gasification, which is squarely 'transmission' as GGIT defines it.

validity.researcher_notes: Operator (АО «Интергаз Центральная Азия») is strongly corroborated: intergas.kz's own 'About the company' page states ICA is the national operator of Kazakhstan's main gas pipeline transmission system and a subsidiary of NC QazaqGaz; the ecoportal.kz environmental filing names ICA's Uralsk LPU (linear production department) as running exactly the 0-152.13km 'Karachaganak-Uralsk' segment; and a Dec 2024 EPSD (state construction-expertise portal) filing for a new looping/2nd-string project on this same pipeline names the client as 'Филиал "Управление магистральных газопроводов 'Уральск'" АО 'Интергаз Центральная Азия'' — i.e. ICA's Uralsk branch is the asset manager commissioning even NEW works on this line today. Owner (QazaqGaz 100%) is weaker: the 2007 Government Decree only commits to eventually transferring pipeline ownership to 'the Republic of Kazakhstan' (the state), not explicitly to QazaqGaz by name, and intergas.kz only establishes that ICA (the operator) is QazaqGaz's subsidiary — that shows corporate parentage, not that QazaqGaz (rather than ICA) holds the pipeline asset itself. Also worth noting for EndLocation precision: the 2007 KazInform piece specifies the actual tie-in point is near the village of Novenkiy, ~15km from Uralsk city, not literally inside Uralsk — GEM's 'Uralsk / West Kazakhstan' end-location is a reasonable city-level simplification, not an error.

validity.researcher_notes: ConstructionYear=2008 does not match the two dated primary sources I found for the actual ground-breaking. Government of Kazakhstan Decree No.1151 authorizing the project's construction is dated 30 November 2007. Independently, the KazInform wire story (via online.zakon.kz/Document/?doc_id=30144485) reports that PM Karim Masimov attended the ceremonial 'opening of construction' ('открытие строительства газопровода') on 23 November 2007 — a week before the Decree. Both are dated, on-point, and from different origins (government legal register vs. news wire quoting the oblast akimat). Neither source is compatible with a 2008 construction start; if anything they place the formal construction launch in November 2007. It is possible full-scale earthworks ramped up into 2008 after the November 2007 ceremony (the article does note ~6M+3M USD of 'preliminary works' funded back in 2006), so I am flagging this as a concern rather than asserting a hard correction, but the weight of dated evidence favors 2007 over 2008.

validity.recommendation: Route to Update: Capacity likely needs to change from 0.50 bcm/y to ~2.52 bcm/y (2,520 million m3/year), sourced to Intergas's own current trunk-pipeline capacity register — a >5x increase from the current sheet value. Do not apply blind; flagging for Update's judgment given the magnitude.
validity.researcher_notes: MAJOR spec discrepancy, found by checking the actual operator's current technical register rather than stopping at the sheet's own vintage of sourcing. GEM's Capacity=0.50 bcm/y (500 million m3/year) traces to 2007 pre-construction planning language: both the KazInform article and the Government Decree describe 'final/ultimate volumes up to 500 million cubic meters per year' as the DESIGN TARGET at the time the project was approved (with an initial ramp-up figure of only 120 million m3/y from the existing gas-treatment unit). However, Intergas Central Asia's own current capacity register — 'Информация о наличии существующей мощности Магистральных Газопроводов АО «Интергаз Центральная Азия», по состоянию на 01.01.2025' (intergas.kz PDF, verified by direct pdftotext/pdfplumber read, not just the url_verifier substring screen which false-negatived on the space-separated '2 520' token) — lists 'Карачаганак-Уральск: диаметр 508мм, протяженность 152км, год ввода 2011' with BOTH Проектная (design) and Фактическая на 2024 (actual-2024) capacity columns reading 2,520 million m3/year (28% utilization in 2024). I verified the column alignment against pdfplumber word x-coordinates row-by-row (matches the same x0 pattern as the neighboring Saryarka row, which is unambiguous in the plain-text extraction) — this is not a misread. A 508mm/20-inch pipe carrying only 500 mcm/y over 152km would be dramatically oversized hydraulically, whereas 2,520 mcm/y is a physically sensible throughput for that diameter — which further supports the 2024 register over the 2007 planning figure as the value that actually reflects what got built. Diameter (508mm) and length (152km, vs. sheet's 152.00) and StartYear1 (2011) all independently CONFIRM against this same register plus the ecoportal.kz filing (152.13km, 2011) — those three fields are fine. Only Capacity is off, and it's off by a lot. Note a secondary complication: a TMK (pipe manufacturer) press release from Dec 2009 about pipe delivered 'for construction of the Karachaganak-Uralsk gas pipeline' lists diameters of 273mm (bulk, 6,000t), 219mm (250t) and 1016mm (1,900t) — none of which is 508mm. Given the 2007 Decree's own text describes the same overall project as including separate high-pressure BRANCH pipelines to two villages (Novopavlovka, Zhympity) in addition to the 152km main line, I read the TMK figures as most likely covering that mixed scope (main line + branches + a large-diameter insert section) rather than being the single nominal diameter of the registered 152km trunk itself — so I did not treat 508mm as a concern, only Capacity.

summary: P3947 Karachaganak-Uralsk Gas Pipeline: existence, classification and non-duplicate status all confirmed via 4+ independent primary sources (2007 Govt Decree No.1151, KazInform wire, TMK pipe-delivery release, and Intergas's own current 01.01.2025 capacity register); Length (152/152.13km), Diameter (508mm) and StartYear1 (2011) all independently confirmed against that same current operator register. Two concerns raised: ConstructionYear=2008 conflicts with dated 2007 primary evidence (Decree + ground-breaking ceremony both Nov 2007), and Capacity=0.50 bcm/y conflicts materially with Intergas's own current register, which lists design+actual capacity at 2,520 million m3/year (2.52 bcm/y) — a >5x discrepancy worth Update's attention. Owner (QazaqGaz) left UNRESOLVED — only Intergas Central Asia is directly documented as running this specific asset.
